text:
maya: Quick question about the /v1/rerank contract — we added `score` and `raw_scores` yesterday. Two quick compatibility/semantics checks: 1) should `score` always be normalized to [0,1], or can it be a raw logit? 2) what is the official tie-break behavior when scores are equal?

kevin: We intended `score` to be a normalized probability in [0,1]. `raw_scores` is the model-specific value (logits or model confidence). Backcompat note: old clients only looked at whatever `score` was and used that for ordering.

priya: If we normalize (softmax) per-response-list, monotonicity is preserved within that request but the absolute values aren't comparable across requests — calling that out in the doc is important. Also small candidate sets + float rounding can flip ties.

sam: Proposed rules: `score` = softmax(raw_scores) across returned candidates for that request. Ordering: sort by `score` desc; if equal within EPS (1e-9), break ties by a deterministic stable key (e.g., `id` asc). If there is `explanation.priority` we can use that before `id` as a secondary tie-breaker.

maya: @sam that softmax approach is great, but note: some existing integrations expect ordering by raw logits. If normalized, their outputs could reorder slightly. Can we add an opt-in to preserve legacy ordering? e.g., query param `?raw_ordering=true` or a header.

ci-bot: :information_source: RFC created: #314 — rerank score semantics and legacy ordering. Action items: docs update, client migrations, tests.

kevin: I like `raw_ordering` as an explicit opt-in. Default should be normalized `score` for two reasons: 1) thresholding is more intuitive, 2) embedding downstream consumers commonly expect [0,1]. We'll add tests for both behaviors.

priya: Add this explicit note to the contract: "Do not compare `score` values across different requests; use them only for intra-response ranking and thresholding." Also recommend clients apply rounding (to e.g., 1e-6) before equality checks to avoid floating jitter.

maya: I'll draft a minimal spec snippet for the docs. Sample request/response to paste into the RFC: 

```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "queries": ["best coffee near me"],
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Coffee shop A"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"Coffee shop B"},
    {"id":"c3","text":"Cafe C"}
  ],
  "params": {"context":"search_v1"}
}

200 OK
{
  "results": [
    {"id":"c2","text":"Coffee shop B","raw_score": 2.1, "score": 0.62},
    {"id":"c1","text":"Coffee shop A","raw_score": 1.2, "score": 0.29},
    {"id":"c3","text":"Cafe C","raw_score": 0.6, "score": 0.09}
  ]
}
```

kevin: Also include the schema snippet in the spec: `results[]` entries have `id` (string), `text` (string), optional `raw_score` (number), required `score` (number between 0 and 1). Add `info.tie_breaker` optional field which will contain the applied tie-break reason ("id", "priority", "raw_ordering").

sam: For the legacy path (when `raw_ordering=true`) define: sort by `raw_score` desc, then `id` asc. Document that in that mode `score` will still be present (softmax of raw) but ordering is by raw. That keeps clients receiving `score` while preserving legacy ordering when requested.

priya: One more edge: streaming rerank responses (partial results) — ensure we don't stream until final scores computed, or else the client may misinterpret partial order as final. Add a note: streaming is unsupported for rerank until we have deterministic partial semantics.

maya: Plan: I'll push a spec PR with the snippets above, add tests for: normalized ordering, raw_ordering opt-in, tie break by `explanation.priority`, and stable `id` fallback. Will canary on staging next Tue. Ping reviewers @kevin @priya when PR is up. :raised_hands:

kevin: ack, will review.

priya: ack — will add a short migration guide for mobile clients.

sam: ping me for canary run, I can flip traffic and watch ordering diffs quickly.

maya: Thanks everyone — doing the PR now, will include example curl and SDK snippets too. :rocket:
